history.summary: A hilltop Shakti shrine on a green hill in the Dewali area overlooking Fateh Sagar Lake, reached by a roughly 900-metre stairway or the monocable ropeway inaugurated in 2024. Tradition dates it to 1652-1680 and attributes it to a Mewar Maharana - travel guides variously name 'Ranjeet Singh I', which is likely a confusion for Maharana Raj Singh I (reigned 1652-1680). The 56-inch stone idol of the goddess is accompanied by a Ganesh idol and three west-facing stone lions, with a hawan kund outside the sanctum. It is described as the kuldevi of the Mewar royal family and, separately, of the Dokot khandan of Bhatnagar Kayasthas; both claims are from online travel writing and are flagged as unverified. Coordinates are a street-level approximation near the hill base, not the exact hilltop. No duplicates of other CSV rows found.

name: Neemach Mata Temple
town_description: Udaipur, the 'City of Lakes' in southern Rajasthan, was founded as the capital of the Mewar kingdom by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559. Set among the Aravalli hills around Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar, it is one of India's most visited heritage cities, known for its palaces, temples and old-city lanes.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur), about 22 km east.
travel.railway: Udaipur City railway station, about 7 km away.
travel.road: The hill base is reached via Fateh Sagar Road / Dewali in the city; from there it is a 900-metre climb on foot or the 2024 ropeway.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Trawell lists 4:30 AM-12:00 PM and 5:00-7:30 PM; other guides list 6:00 AM-8:00 PM. Timings vary with season and festivals - verify on arrival. Ropeway round trip about Rs 185-200 per person (2024-25 figures).
